purpose: Synchronised wake-word stimulus plus an audible loopback check, with both I2S input channels reported separately.

part_a_wake_word.window: one reset at 18:18:46 followed by 60s + 45s of continuous capture (105s total)

user_stimulus.instruction: stay silent for ~10s, then face the device at 20-30cm and say the wake word 4 times, >=3s apart
user_stimulus.user_confirmed_manner: spoken directly at the device, normal volume
user_stimulus.source: user answered '6 times' when asked after the window

part_a_wake_word.detections_vs_utterances: 6 detections for 6 confirmed utterances; no surplus detection, so this window is not evidence of a false trigger
part_a_wake_word.latch_observation: HEALTH at 100014 ms shows wake=0 while detection 6 is at 99578 ms and its re-arm is at 100734 ms. This is the first direct confirmation that wake= is a latch cleared by a detection, matching the source reading, rather than a steady status bit.

part_b_loopback.window: no reset; 60s + 30s immediately after part A
part_b_loopback.user_confirmed_taps: 2; the first cycle falls in the uncaptured gap t=106.7s..147.3s between part A and part B
part_b_loopback.user_reported_audibility: heard own voice played back, clear and normal volume

reference_channel_finding.observation: Channel 1, the slot the board declares as the playback reference, reported rms=0 peak=0 raw_peak=1 in all 87 windows of the loopback round and all 96 windows of the wake round; it never moved, including while audio was playing.
source_evidence: integration/v6/board/claw4-learning-v6/claw4_audio.cc:14-15 declares input_reference_ = true and input_channels_ = 2 ('Metalio interleaved microphone / playback reference').
claw4_audio.cc:79 maps the I2S word index parity onto the channel, so channel 1 is whatever the codec puts in the second Rx slot.
claw4_audio.cc:128 fills both Tx slots with the same sample, so the transmit path never feeds a reference; the reference has to come from the codec/slip-ring hardware.
The AFE pipeline in the same build is |AEC(FD_LOW_COST, NLP_VERY_AGGRESSIVE)| -> |VAD(WebRTC)| -> |WakeNet(...)|, so an AEC stage is enabled and expects a reference signal.
reference_channel_finding.conclusion: In this build the declared reference channel carries no data. Whatever the AEC stage consumes as reference, it is not this channel. I did not change any gain, codec setting or code.
reference_channel_finding.impact: For M1 the device plays TTS while the microphone keeps listening; on this evidence the echo path cannot be cancelled, which is the same self-hearing failure mode seen earlier in V5.3. It also means the loopback audio the user heard is not evidence that AEC works.
reference_channel_finding.not_claimed: I do not claim the hardware is incapable: the reference may need a codec loopback setting, a different slot, or a software echo path. That is Codex's call.

clipping_finding.observation: Channel 0 keeps clipping at int16 full scale while the user speaks.
clipping_finding.arithmetic: The largest raw_peak observed anywhere in these four captures is 2147418112 (cp2-loopback-01.txt at 159196 ms), which is 0.0031% below 2^31. 2^31 >> 12 = 524288, sixteen times the int16 ceiling of 32767, so clipping is forced; 2^31 >> 16 = 32768, i.e. exactly full scale. All window values here are read from the logs, not transcribed by hand.
clipping_finding.conclusion: The int32-to-int16 shift of 12 over-gains by 16x. This round reproduces it from an independent capture and gives the numeric basis for shifting by 16 instead.
clipping_finding.subjective_vs_objective: The user reports the loopback playback is clear and at a normal volume, so the audible loopback alone would not have surfaced this. Clipping and audibility are reported as separate items.
clipping_finding.action_taken: None. No gain or threshold was changed; this is Codex's decision.
clipping_finding.note_on_attribution: An earlier draft of this file attributed two of the worst windows to cp2-loopback-02.txt; they are actually in cp2-wake-02.txt. The values are now extracted programmatically so no window is attributed by hand.

distortion_and_volume.objective: The recorded frame was captured with 3 to 1098 clipped samples per second in the loudest seconds, and the playback volume uses volume^2 scaling with factor 65536 at volume=100, i.e. unity.

vad.note: Consistent with the firmware banner: wake-only never calls HandleVoiceResult, so a missing VAD event is not evidence about level.

health_flat.note: Recorded here only as raw values; the long-run trend belongs to CP3.

bounds_of_this_result: The loopback audible check bypasses the AFE: AudioService copies channel 0 into the testing queue, so it exercises microphone -> codec -> speaker and nothing else.
Only one of the user's two loopback cycles was captured; the other falls in a documented capture gap.
Six detections for six utterances says the wake word fires under these conditions; it is not a wake rate and no threshold is claimed.
The elevated channel 0 level that follows the playback queue event cannot be separated into speaker pickup and user voice from level numbers alone.
